security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU TCG incorrectly applies capability integrity checks (e.g., canonicalization, reserved-bit clearing, field normalization) to the data loaded by a capability load instruction when the source capability's tag is zero. The spec mandates that all YLEN bits must transfer unmutated through registers, even if the bit pattern contains reserved-bit violations or would fail integrity invariants.
security_spec.summary: Capability load with zero tag must bypass all integrity canonicalization in QEMU TCG — applying reserved-bit clearing or field normalization on untagged loads silently corrupts guest capability-oblivious memcpy()

findings.finding: No CHERI capability emulation code exists anywhere in this QEMU repository (branch master). The capability load/decode/canonicalization vulnerability pattern described in the security spec does not apply because the code to be analyzed does not exist. Searched for: cheri, cap_load, cap_decode, cap_tag, cap_metadata, cap_perms, cap_bounds, cap_otype, load_cap, Cload, Cstore, cget, canonicalization of capabilities across the entire target/ directory and the whole repository — all returned zero results.
